$comment: The one home of villanelle's public API: every concept with its typed members, the kind lists, keywords, limits, patterns, error groups and free functions (spec/spec.md and spec/contract.md are canonical for behaviour; this file for the shapes). Types are written in the closed type grammar of spec/codegen.md section 2 and every name must resolve; spec/schema/api.schema.json checks the shape and tools/api/loader.py the rest. Names are spec names (lowercase words); each binding's spelling is derived from them by its casing rule (spec/binding-guide.md rule 1), never stored. Idiom that differs by language is a typed trait (spec/codegen.md section 3), never prose. History (removed names, settled disagreements) is in .claude/design/consumer-api/round15/schema-history.json.

layers.name: shared
layers.holds: positions, places, origins, diagnostics and the diagnostics sink, error groups, the kind lists

layers.name: io
layers.holds: the document source and writer ports, their adapters, and check lost updates (the one lost-update check every writer calls)

layers.name: written
layers.holds: the low level: processor, document graph, documents, statements, values, variables, the expansion and its expanded values with their readers, the extension port and the include extension (spec 5: an extension is pure, so it belongs to the layer that owns expansion)

layers.name: rendered
layers.holds: the rendered tree: render (graph), directives, arguments, addresses, diff

layer direction: A layer imports only the layers in its 'may import' list; nothing below the rendered layer imports, names or returns a rendered type (owner, 2026-10-29: "The low level shouldn't \"depend on\" the middle layer"). Going up a layer is the upper layer's free function: render (graph).

token kind.note: the grammar's lexer rule names (fragments aside) in declaration order: the grammar is their one home, and they are the one list whose values are not lowercase words

value kind.note: the written value variants cover the whole list; an expanded value's variants cover it less 'reference'

unreadable reason.note: computed by the low level's expansion (spec 6.10); 'unread' marks an extension copy not read yet (E3007)

walk control.note: what a walk's callback returns to pass over an item's block or end the walk (TypeScript's walk idiom; Python's walk is a generator, so break ends it and descend passes over a block)

limits.name: nesting depth
limits.means: blocks and lists nested at most this deep

limits.name: expansion depth
limits.means: use and extension lines nested at most this deep

limits.name: integer range
limits.means: integer words and slice or index bounds lie within plus or minus this (2^53-1)

reserved names.means: the language statements' names, written @set, @snippet and @use: no extension may take one (spec 2.5, 5). Milestone 5: no directive name is reserved any more; a directive's name is a WORD, which never starts with @

variable name.means: a $name without its $, an override name, a variable rename

program code.means: <namespace>/<name>, a program's own diagnostic code: both parts non-empty, no whitespace (the Unicode White_Space set, written out so JavaScript and Python agree); villanelle's codes start with E

error groups.name: villanelle error
error groups.raised when: never by itself: the base class of every expected-outcome class (spec 2.8), so one except or catch clause catches every outcome the input or the outside world decides, and no program bug

error groups.name: diagnostic error
error groups.raised when: a reader is given a value of the wrong kind or spelling, or a program's error(...); carries one located diagnostic as 'diagnostic'

error groups.name: read error
error groups.raised when: load cannot resolve the root path to exactly one file, or cannot read it. No diagnostic and no code

error groups.name: bad text error
error groups.raised when: the text given to an edit, or an override's text, is not what its entry rule (spec 2.8) and the text-alone rules take; 'diagnostics' are located in that text, in the binding's string unit; its message is built from them (spec 2.8)

error groups.name: lost update error
error groups.raised when: a file the save would write changed since it was read or last saved: its current text differs from its saved text (spec 4.2). Raised by check lost updates inside every writer; save raises it as is
error groups.note: paths are only the conflicting files, in batch order

error groups.name: detached error
error groups.raised when: any member but kind of a detached handle is used

error groups.name: argument type error
error groups.raised when: an argument of the wrong type: anything but text where config text or a name is taken (an extension's name at make processor included), and to quote and text (spec 6.9), a writer that is not a document writer, a render given something that is not a document graph (no callable expand; spec 7.0, milestone 5), a key rule that returns anything but text or absent (spec 7.4)

error groups.name: misuse error
error groups.raised when: a bad argument value a program could have checked: every bad name (a variable or override name not matching the variable name pattern; a directive rename, or an extension's name at make processor, that the nameText entry rule refuses), a program code without '/', a reserved (set, snippet, use) or repeated extension name

error groups.name: index out of range
error groups.raised when: an insert index outside a block; a token range outside a parse

argument type error message.rule: One helper per binding builds it (one home); every member that takes config text, quote, text, rename, set override, each load override and render call it before changing anything. Messages are for people (spec 2.3); the class and the member and parameter named are the contract.
argument type error message.ts: {member}(): argument "{parameter}" must be a string, not {got}; villanelle edits take config text: quote() a program string, text() one already written as villanelle text, String() a number first
argument type error message.py: {member}() argument '{parameter}' must be str, not {got}; villanelle edits take config text: quote() a program string, text() one already written as villanelle text, str() a number first
argument type error message.got: the argument's type as the language names it: TypeScript null, array or typeof; Python type(value).__name__
argument type error message.member: the member in the binding's casing, as the caller wrote it: set, replaceWithText / replace_with_text, insertStatements / insert_statements, addStatements / add_statements, insertBefore / insert_before, insertAfter / insert_after, setOverride / set_override, rename, quote, load, text, render
argument type error message.parameter: text; name for rename and for set override's name; overrides["<name>"] for a load override; raw for text; graph for render
argument type error message.other: a parameter that takes something other than text names what it takes instead of 'a string' / 'str'

free functions.name: span of
free functions.note: a pure helper over a syntax value (spec 1, 'Where an operation lives', rule 4); stays a free function in milestone 1

free functions.name: text of
free functions.note: a pure helper over a syntax value (spec 1, 'Where an operation lives', rule 4); stays a free function in milestone 1

free functions.name: quote
free functions.note: returns config text (spec 6.9, milestone 5): the text written as a villanelle string, escapes included

free functions.name: text
free functions.note: milestone 5 (vil-umh.6): raw as config text, unchanged and unchecked: the program's statement that raw is already written as villanelle text; the edit it is given checks it. With quote, the only maker of config text

free functions.name: render
free functions.note: the rendered layer's entry point: going up a layer is a free function of the upper layer (owner, 2026-10-29). Pure: reads no file. Builds only on the low level's public members (document graph expand (), spec 7.0). Exported only by the rendered layer's namespace (binding guide rule 9). Given anything without a callable expand it raises the argument type error first (milestone 5)

free functions.name: format diagnostic
free functions.note: takes a document graph (a written type), so it belongs to the low level, not shared; was listed as shared in the first draft of this file

free functions.name: memory source
free functions.note: reads the map it is given at each call, never a copy: what a memory writer puts in the same map, a later load reads

free functions.name: memory writer
free functions.note: writes each batch into the map it is given (the one a memory source reads), refusing a lost update as the file writer does: nothing is written when a file's text in the map (empty when absent) differs from its saved text

free functions.name: check lost updates

params.name: current
params.note: each file's text in the medium now, in the order of files; absent when there is none (read as empty text)

free functions.note: the one lost-update check (spec 4.2): raises a lost update error whose paths are the files whose current text differs from their saved text, in batch order. Every writer calls it before it writes; a program's own writer should too

concepts.name: config text
concepts.note: milestone 5 (vil-umh.6; owner, 2026-10-29: "Yes, its own type"): villanelle text a program hands to an edit or an override, made only by quote or text; every edit's and override's text parameter takes it, so a plain string there is a type error the checker reports. Still the language's string at run time

concepts.name: expanded value
concepts.note: a union: one value after expansion ($name replaced) with its links to the lines it came through. The low level owns it (spec 2.9, 6.10): an extension use holds it, a directive expansion's values are it, and a rendered directive's values are the same objects (milestone 4 collapsed value expansion and the rendered argument family into it). The readers stay on every variant: a value of the wrong kind is a problem in the config text, reported as E4002. Two expanded values are equal exactly when their texts are equal (spec 2.9; Python ==)

members.name: written
members.note: the written value on the same line: chain[0].reference when the value came through a variable (a list item that came through one shares its list's), else the value itself; never absent. Was value expansion's and the rendered argument's written

members.name: definition
members.note: the written value at the end of the chain; absent for an override

members.name: chain
members.note: one per variable step of origin.via, own line first; empty when read where written

members.name: list
